newsitem.title: USA: GASB seeks key changes to local finance reporting.
newsitem.headline: GASB seeks key changes to local finance reporting.

text.p: The Governmental Accounting Standards Board said Monday they had proposed major revisions to the way state and local governments will report on their finances beginning in the next century.

For the first time, investors will be better able to tell from financial statements whether a state or local government has sufficient revenues to pay for current services, the GASB said in a statement.
The GASB is a private-sector panel that sets financial accounting and reporting standards for states and localities.

The GASB asked for comments on the proposal, titled Basic Financial Statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis for State and Local Governments, by May 30. It said public hearings are set for June, July, and August.

"Our proposal is intended to make governments' financial reports easier to understand and more useful to the citizenry, investors, creditors, and legislative bodies, especially if they have no experience using them before," GASB Chairman Tom L. Allen said.

"Right now, governments show their finances based only on 'fund accounting,'" Allen said. "There is a general fund, which typically is used to account for things like police and fire protection in local government and public assistance in state government."
"But a government can have virtually an unlimited number of other funds, such as special revenue funds for state and highway maintenance, all presented separately," Allen added.
"As a result, it is difficult for many people to understand how all the funds fit together," he said. "All that (would) change under the GASB's new proposal."
The new proposal would require governments to show all of their operations, like police, fire, and water and sewerage, in one place, which the GASB calls an "entity-wide perspective."

Municipalities would have to prepare financial statements using the "accrual basis" of accounting, similar to that used by most businesses, the GASB said. It said its new financial reporting model also would require a "management's discussion and analysis" in financial reports.

"The board envisions here a brief, objective, and easily readable analysis of the government's financial activities written with an average reader in mind, one not necessarily possessing a detailed knowledge of accounting," Allen said.
Teh proposal is the culmination of years of research and public input, he said.
Copies of the proposal are available from the GASB Order Department, 401 Merritt 7, PO Box 5116, Norwalk, CT 06856-5116, or by calling 203-847-0700, ext. 555, the GASB said.
